title: Committee of Supply – Head U (Prime Minister's Office)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head U (Prime Minister's Office)

sections.label: Budget funds for climate change
sections.summary: The Government set aside Budget funds for climate change, including $5 billion for coastal and flood protection, amid a public health crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Too often, it is a flashy speech or some performative act that grabs attention for a brief moment and then it is back to business as usual.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: So, it is heartening that even in the middle of a high profile and salient public health crisis, our Government has set aside funds in the Budget to deal with climate change, including $5 billion for coastal and flood protection measures.

sections.label: Cross-sector collaboration and infrastructure guidelines
sections.summary: Energy and waste efficiency need collaboration across housing and transport, and critical infrastructure like air and seaports must be at least four metres above sea level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: For example, efficiency in energy consumption and waste disposal requires there to be strong collaboration across the housing and transport sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We have already put in place guidelines for critical infrastructure, such as air and seaports, to be at least four metres above sea level.

sections.label: Carbon scheme and waste-to-energy plants
sections.summary: The Carbon Emissions-based Vehicle Scheme has been launched, and Waste-to-Energy plants reduce waste volumes by 90% and convert waste to reusable energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In policy, the Carbon Emissions-based Vehicle Scheme has been launched.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In business, Waste-to-Energy plants reduce waste volumes by 90% and allow conversion to reusable energy.

sections.label: Solar share of generation capacity
sections.summary: Currently, 1.3% of Singapore's generation capacity comes from solar photovoltaic generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Currently, 1.3% of Singapore’s generation capacity is from solar photovoltaic (PV) generation.

sections.label: Fossil fuels and economic strategy
sections.summary: Fossil fuels are estimated at 3% of Singapore's GDP, and weaning off them requires a fundamental change to Singapore's economic strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The fossil fuels business is estimated to be 3% of Singapore's gross domestic product (GDP).

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Weaning off fossil fuels requires a fundamental change to Singapore's economic strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The current generation would have to foot the coastal protection bill, but they might not live to see the benefits.

sections.label: Regional clean power transmission lines
sections.summary: Building transmission lines to neighbours would let land-scarce Singapore tap clean power and reduce fossil fuel reliance for electricity generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With spare land to install solar panels or wind turbines, something practically impossible to undertake on a large enough scale in land-scarce Singapore, building transmission lines to connect to our neighbours would allow Singapore to readily tap on clean power and significantly reduce our reliance for fossil fuels for electricity generation.

sections.label: Antarctic record temperature reading
sections.summary: A Brazilian-run research station recorded an extreme temperature of 20.75 degrees celsius in the Antarctic on 9 February 2020.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: On 9 February 2020, a Brazilian-run research station recorded an extreme temperature of 20.75 degrees celsius in the Antarctic.

sections.label: ASEAN emissions and renewables financing
sections.summary: The biggest environment problem among some ASEAN members is plans to increase projects emitting large amounts of carbon, and the way forward is boosting slow renewables financing in ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The biggest environment problem amongst some ASEAN members is the plan to increase such projects, which will emit large amounts of carbon into the atmosphere, and I think that the way forward is to boost renewables financing in ASEAN, which is currently taking place at a very slow rate.

sections.label: Carbon Pricing Act effectiveness doubt
sections.summary: The Carbon Pricing Act took effect last year, but some doubt carbon taxing in Singapore guarantees the desired level of emissions reduction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: One key effort was passing the Carbon Pricing Act, which took effect last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, there has been some doubt about the effectiveness of carbon taxing in Singapore as some say it does not guarantee the desired level of emissions reduction.

sections.label: Review against holistic progress indicators
sections.summary: A review is proposed to measure absolute carbon emission levels against holistic progress indicators, noting a public consultation on Singapore's long-term low-emissions strategy whose findings were released in early February.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can the Government consider a review to measure absolute carbon emission levels against holistic progress indicators, such as the Human Development Index or the United Nations Environment Inclusive Wealth Index?

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I note that the Government had also carried out a public consultation exercise last year to discuss formulating Singapore's long-term low-emissions development strategy and the findings were released in early February.

sections.label: Singapore submitting NDC and LEDS
sections.summary: Later this year Singapore will submit its enhanced 2030 Nationally Determined Contribution to the Paris Agreement and its Long-Term Low Emissions Development Strategy for 2050 and beyond to the UNFCCC.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Later this year, Singapore will submit our enhanced 2030 Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) to the Paris Agreement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: We will also submit our Long-Term Low Emissions Development Strategy (LEDS) for 2050 and beyond to the United Nations (UN) Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

sections.label: Enhanced NDC and NF3 reporting
sections.summary: Singapore will enhance its 2030 NDC by committing to an absolute peak emission level of 65 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent around 2030, and will include NF3 in its pledge.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: In 2015, we set our 2030 NDC target to reduce our emissions intensity in 2030 by 36% from 2005 levels, and to peak by around 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam will be glad to know we will be enhancing our NDC by committing to an absolute peak emission level of 65 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent around 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: All countries are also now required to report on the 7th greenhouse gas, Nitrogen Trifluoride (NF3) by 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: We will go beyond reporting NF3, and commit to including NF3 in our pledge, within this same emissions ceiling.

sections.label: Long-Term Low Emissions Strategy
sections.summary: The strategy aims to halve emissions from the 2030 peak to 33 million tonnes by 2050, targeting net-zero as soon as viable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Our Long-Term Low Emissions Development Strategy aspires to halve the emissions from our 2030 peak, to 33 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent by 2050, with a view to achieving net-zero emissions as soon as viable in the second half of the century.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: This will be very challenging, given our limited alternative energy options.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: We have studied the matter very carefully and developed a strategy to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: First, we need transformations in our industry, economy and society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Second, we have to draw on technologies which are not yet mature, such as carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS), and low carbon fuels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And third, we will need international collaboration in areas, such as well-functioning carbon markets and regional electricity grids.

sections.label: Solar Deployment Acceleration
sections.summary: Solar deployment is being accelerated from 350 MWp by end of this year to at least two GWp by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: While we are limited in hydro, wind and nuclear energy, we are pressing ahead with solar deployment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: We are significantly accelerating our deployment of solar, from 350 megawatt peak (MWp) by the end of this year, to at least two gigawatt-peak (GWp) by 2030.

sections.label: Carbon Tax Revenue
sections.summary: The carbon tax will collect roughly $1 billion over the first five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The carbon tax, which we have introduced, will collect roughly $1 billion over the first five years.

sections.label: Walk Cycle Ride Journeys
sections.summary: Investments in public transport and active mobility aim for nine in 10 peak period journeys by Walk, Cycle, Ride by 2040.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Major investments in public transport and active mobility infrastructure will pave the way for nine in 10 of all peak period journeys to be made using "Walk, Cycle, Ride" transport modes by 2040.

sections.label: Phasing Out ICE Vehicles
sections.summary: Internal combustion engine vehicles will be phased out by 2040, with all vehicles running on cleaner energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: As announced by Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat, we will phase out internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles by 2040 and have all vehicles running on cleaner energy.

sections.label: Energy-Efficient LED Bulbs
sections.summary: With all light bulbs as efficient as LED bulbs from 2023, households save about $3.5 million annually and cut emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: With all our light bulbs as energy-efficient as light emitting diode (LED) bulbs from 2023, our households will save about $3.5 million annually in energy costs and reduce carbon emissions by around 6.3 million kilotonnes annually.

sections.label: MAS green investments programme
sections.summary: MAS established a US$2 billion green investments programme to anchor green activities of asset managers in Singapore and support mainstreaming of green finance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) recently established a US$2 billion green investments programme to anchor green activities of asset managers in Singapore and support the mainstreaming of green finance.

sections.label: Sea level rise reclamation platform
sections.summary: Singapore raised the platform level for all reclamation projects by one metre, from three to four metres above the Singapore Height Datum, in 2011.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: On the one hand, our impact on global emissions is small but, on the other hand, the effect of climate change on us is disproportionately large and, indeed, existential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: We must thus plan seriously for the real prospect that sea levels will rise by up to one metre by 2100, in line with what climate science is telling us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: In 2011, we raised the platform level for all reclamation projects by an additional one metre, from three metres to four metres above the Singapore Height Datum (SHD).

sections.label: Changi Airport Terminal 5 platform
sections.summary: For key new facilities such as Changi Airport Terminal 5, the platform level is being raised to at least five metres above SHD.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: For key new facilities, such as Changi Airport Terminal 5, we are raising the platform level even higher, to at least five metres above SHD.

sections.label: Coastal and Flood Protection Fund
sections.summary: Prime Minister Lee estimated sea level rise plans will cost $100 billion over 100 years, and DPM Heng announced a Coastal and Flood Protection Fund with an initial $5 billion top-up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: In his National Day Rally speech last year, Prime Minister Lee outlined the threats from sea level rise and our plans estimating that this will cost $100 billion over the next 100 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat announced in the Budget a new Coastal and Flood Protection Fund, with an initial top-up of $5 billion to start setting aside the resources that we will need for this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: We have divided our coastal areas into hydraulically-distinct segments to study different options for each area.

sections.label: Singapore total population 2019
sections.summary: According to the Department of Statistics, Singapore's total population stands at 5.703 million as of 2019.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, according to the Department of Statistics, Singapore's total population stands at 5.703 million as of 2019.

sections.label: Old-age support ratio decline
sections.summary: The old-age support ratio declined from 4.8 in 2018 to 4.5 in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: What is worrisome is the decline of old-age support ratio from 4.8 in 2018 to 4.5 in 2019.

sections.label: Resident TFR numbers falling
sections.summary: Population in Brief 2019 shows Chinese and Indian resident TFRs fell to about 0.98 and one, down from 1.14 and 1.19 a decade ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The vast majority of residents are permanently invested in this country and do not have the luxury of imagining a home away from Singapore, nor would we have it that way.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: However, the Population in Brief 2019 data released by the PMO Strategy Group reveals that the TFR numbers for the Chinese and Indian residents have fallen to around 0.98 and one respectively, compared to 1.14 and 1.19 a decade ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: From a high of 1.91 in 2008, the number fell to 1.66 in 2013, before steadily and consistently moving up to 1.85 in 2018.

sections.label: Immigration from non-traditional countries
sections.summary: It asks whether population plans may change to attract immigrants from non-traditional countries, which were about 6.3% of citizenships and PRs granted in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Does this anticipate some changes to our population plans with a desire to attract immigrants from further afield, specifically non-traditional countries classified as "others", which currently account for about 6.3% of Singapore citizenships and PRs granted in 2018, as compared to 62.5% from Southeast Asian countries and 31.2% from Asian countries?

sections.label: Equity for non-working mothers
sections.summary: It hopes non tax-related benefits, such as early childhood education subsidies and child relief, can be more equal between working and non-working mothers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Whether in or outside of employment, mothers play an important role in our society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So, in all our non tax-related benefits, such as for early childhood education subsidies, child relief amongst others, I hope that we can have more equity between working and non-working mothers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: There will be some benefits that we will need to segregate and have some amount of additional help for those who have children but have decided to go back into the workforce, but the rest, especially, benefits for the children, should be equalised.

sections.label: Support for marriage and parenthood
sections.summary: It asks how Government enhancements supporting marriage and parenthood have benefited young Singaporeans and what measures encourage an increase in TFR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Some areas that are often talked about are flexible work arrangements (FWAs), having a conducive work culture, parental leave and, importantly, increased childcare leave and more childcare leave for the mothers and the fathers who have more children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: How have the enhancements provided by the Government to support marriage and parenthood benefited young Singaporeans and their families?

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: What measures are we putting in place to encourage an increase in our TFR?

sections.label: Measures for ageing and low TFR
sections.summary: It states that enhancing marriage and parenthood is critical to ageing population and low TFR problems, and that the Government rolled out measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Enhancing marriage and parenthood is critical to addressing our ageing population and low TFR problems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Government has rolled out important measures, such as shortening the time to get housing and defraying child-raising costs.

sections.label: Flexible work and childcare leave
sections.summary: It says allowing 40,000 women to go on FWA yearly must be manageable and that childcare leave provisions should be reviewed again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: If businesses could do it for large swathes of the workforce during the outbreak now, certainly allowing 40,000 women to go on FWA each year must be manageable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It has been more than a decade since childcare leave provisions were increased and it is time to review this again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Public Service already gives officers childcare sick leave and it is on a per child basis.

sections.label: Singles caring for elderly parents
sections.summary: Some singles may need flexibility to care for elderly parents, and the speaker hopes flexible work arrangements become more pervasive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Some singles may also have elderly parents to care for and need the flexibility to take some time to perhaps bring their parents for check-ups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am grateful for the Government's efforts in giving out the Work-Life Grant and in encouraging employers to adopt FWAs, but I believe we would all like to see the adoption of such arrangements to be more pervasive.

sections.label: Total fertility rate below replacement
sections.summary: Singapore's total fertility rate is below replacement, at 1.14 for last year and the year before.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Similar to most developed economies, our TFR is below replacement – at 1.14 for last year and the year before.

sections.label: Births and overseas Singaporean babies
sections.summary: From 2015 to 2019 there were around 33,000 births annually, plus about 1,600 Singaporean babies born overseas each year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: From 2015 to 2019, we had around 33,000 births annually.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This is higher than the average from 2010 to 2014, of around 32,000 births annually.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: On top of this, as some Singaporeans live overseas, we welcomed about 1,600 Singaporean babies born overseas each year, over the past five years.

sections.label: Citizen marriages over five years
sections.summary: The average number of citizen marriages in the last five years is higher than previous five-year periods.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Similarly, the average number of citizen marriages in the last five years is higher than previous five-year periods.

sections.label: Childcare cost at Anchor Operator
sections.summary: After subsidies, a working couple earning a combined $5,000 a month pays $130 monthly per child for full-day childcare at an Anchor Operator preschool.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Today, after subsidies, a working couple who earn a combined $5,000 a month, pays $130 per month per child for full-day childcare at an Anchor Operator preschool.

sections.label: Preschool places by 2025
sections.summary: By around 2025, eight in 10 preschoolers can have a place in a Government-supported preschool, up from just over five in 10 today.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: By around 2025, eight in 10 preschoolers can have a place in a Government-supported preschool, up from just over five in 10 today.

sections.label: Housing grants for first-timers
sections.summary: First-timer families receive up to $80,000 for new HDB flats and up to $160,000 for resale flats, with about 1,000 families benefiting from EHG.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: First-timer families now receive up to $80,000 in grants when purchasing a new HDB flat, and up to $160,000 when purchasing an HDB resale flat.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Since its inception, about 1,000 first-timer families have benefited from EHG.

sections.label: Permanent HR leave provision
sections.summary: It will be formalised as a permanent human resource leave provision within the Public Service.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: As such, we will formalise it as a permanent human resource (HR) leave provision within the Public Service.

sections.label: Support for work-life harmony
sections.summary: The Government and tripartite partners support the Panel's intent for better work-life harmony by making it easy, known and accepted.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Government and tripartite partners fully support the Panel’s intent to create conditions for better work-life harmony, and will do so by "making it easy", "making it known" and "making it accepted".

sections.label: Our Singapore Fund support
sections.summary: MCCY will provide support through Our Singapore Fund for Singaporeans organising projects that encourage these shifts.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) will provide support through Our Singapore Fund, for Singaporeans who wish to organise meaningful projects that encourage these shifts.

sections.label: Citizenship and PR grants
sections.summary: Over five years, about 22,100 new citizenships and 31,700 Permanent Residencies were granted yearly on average, with the PR population around half a million.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Over the past five years, we granted about 22,100 new Singapore Citizenships on average each year.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We also granted about 31,700 Permanent Residencies on average each year.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We have kept the total size of the PR population at around half a million for many years now.

sections.label: Population in 2030
sections.summary: Total population in 2030 is likely to be significantly below 6.9 million, and the Government will chart a cohesive and vibrant way forward.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: As I informed the House then, our total population in 2030 – at the end of this decade – is likely to be significantly below 6.9 million.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, on population matters, there are no easy solutions but the Government will do its best to chart the way forward that keeps our society cohesive and our economy vibrant.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We will always have Singaporeans' best interests at heart, now and in the future, and we will never stop progressing as one united people.

sections.label: Singapore Smart Nation recognition
sections.summary: Singapore launched the Smart Nation initiative in November 2014 and is ranked the smartest city in the 2019 IMD Smart City Index.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Singapore has been at the forefront of digital transformation since we launched the Smart Nation initiative in November 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Today, Singapore is globally recognised as a smart city, with the Institute for Management Development (IMD) Smart City Index ranking Singapore as the smartest city in 2019, and several other reputable organisations also place Singapore within the top 10 smart cities globally.

sections.label: Lift monitoring and BIM digitalisation
sections.summary: A telemonitoring system and lift performance dashboard monitor 24,000 lifts in 15 PAP Town Councils, and over 90 blocks were digitalised using BIM.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Third, a telemonitoring system (TMS) for the monitoring of lift breakdowns and also a lift performance dashboard management system to monitor and improve the reliability and safety of 24,000 lifts in the 15 PAP Town Councils.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: For example, we have digitalised over 90 blocks of our flats using Building Information Modelling (BIM) to build a digital database of as-built drawings to facilitate and augment maintenance and improvement works.

sections.label: Facial analysis camera trial
sections.summary: A new camera system could analyse faces by race, gender and age, with a trial planned at one-north and Geylang.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The new camera system was able to analyse faces down to race, gender and age, and a trial was to be held at one-north and Geylang before the project could potentially be extended to more than 100,000 lamp posts in Singapore.

sections.label: Data security breaches and recommendations
sections.summary: HIV-positive individuals' and blood donors' data were compromised, and the PSDSRC's recommendations are to be fully implemented by 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: First, the personal information of more than 14,200 HIV-positive individuals and there was also a case of a loophole in the Health Sciences Authority's (HSA's) system resulting in the compromise of data that affected more than 800,000 blood donors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I understand the Public Sector Data Security Review Committee (PSDSRC) has submitted a slew of recommendations to the Government last November and the Government has accepted those recommendations, which are to be fully implemented by 2023.

sections.label: GoBusiness Licensing Portal for food industry
sections.summary: The GoBusiness Licensing Portal launched in October 2019 lets food industry owners apply with one form of 90 data fields instead of 14 forms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
sentences.text: With the launch of the GoBusiness Licensing Portal by GovTech in October 2019, business owners in the food industry now experience a seamless application process that requires only one form with 90 data fields instead of 14 forms with 845 data fields.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
sentences.text: Also, what are the future plans on the rollout of the integrated licensing portal to other industries?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
sentences.text: What will be the expected savings from these efforts?

sections.label: MyInfo and citizen applications
sections.summary: Building blocks such as MyInfo are in place, and applications like OneService, Parking.SG and Moments of Life offer conveniences to citizens.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Apart from blueprints and action frameworks, basic "building blocks", such as MyInfo, on which personalised services and applications can be built are in place.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We have experienced applications, such as OneService, Parking.SG and Moments of Life, offering conveniences to citizens as we go about our daily lives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Moments of Life, for example, allows me to monitor what vaccinations my two sons have specifically taken and will have to take coming up.

sections.label: OneService citizen voting idea
sections.summary: A suggestion that OneService could let citizens vote on Home Improvement Programmes or block colour schemes during cyclical Repair and Redecorations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: For example, instead of just giving feedback, could we enhance the OneService to allow citizens to vote on Home Improvement Programmes or the colour schemes for their block during the cyclical Repair and Redecorations?

sections.label: Our Singapore Fund Digital Readiness update
sections.summary: A request for an update on the use of Our Singapore Fund for Digital Readiness and its results in cultivating digitally ready citizens.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Could the Government give an update on the use of Our Singapore Fund for Digital Readiness so far?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: What are some of the fruits of our labour in cultivating digitally ready citizens?

sections.label: Birth registration app results
sections.summary: The app is estimated to cut total waiting time from 60 to 15 minutes, and births registered through it rose from 2,000 to almost 20,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: By having this app, we estimated we are able to reduce the total waiting time and all that from 60 minutes to 15 minutes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Last year, I shared that 2,000 births had been registered through this app.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: A year on, this number has increased tenfold, now almost 20,000.

sections.label: Digital MCs issued
sections.summary: Over 400,000 digital MCs have been issued for patients visiting SingHealth hospitals or polyclinics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Today, we have issued over 400,000 digital MCs for all patients who visit SingHealth hospitals or polyclinics.

sections.label: National AI Strategy commitment
sections.summary: The ability to use AI must be made available to everyone, so Singapore is embarking on a National AI Strategy, working with companies and the research community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: And in the same way that computing and communication were made available to all, we need to make this ability available to everyone – people and businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: That is why we have to embark on our own National AI Strategy for Singapore and I give Members this commitment that we are working with companies and the research community to focus our efforts on deploying AI.

sections.label: CPF online nomination service
sections.summary: The service has close to one million users, and since January over 9,000 CPF members and their witnesses completed the process online.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Today, it has close to one million users.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: For example, since CPF launched its online nomination service in January, over 9,000 CPF members and their witnesses have used it to complete the entire process online, securely and conveniently.

sections.label: MyInfo business transaction savings
sections.summary: Businesses report saving up to $50 per transaction and processing five times faster when customers use MyInfo to prefill forms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Businesses also report saving up to $50 per transaction and processing transactions five times faster when their customers use MyInfo to prefill forms.

sections.label: PayNow registration among Singaporeans
sections.summary: Over three-quarters of Singaporeans aged 20 to 75 are registered with PayNow.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Today, over three-quarters of Singaporeans between the age of 20 and 75 are registered with PayNow.

sections.label: CPF withdrawals using PayNow
sections.summary: Last year, 20,000 CPF members made over 90,000 CPF withdrawals via PayNow, transferring over $600 million in real time.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: For instance, last year, 20,000 CPF members conducted over 90,000 CPF withdrawals using PayNow, which amounted to over $600 million being transferred almost instantly, in real time.

sections.label: Punggol smart technologies testbed
sections.summary: Punggol Town will test smart technologies like the Open Digital Platform and smart energy grids, with more details later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Punggol Town will be our testbed to implement smart technologies, such as the Open Digital Platform and smart energy grids in our towns.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Later this year, we will share more about how smart features in residential estates and community facilities will benefit Punggol residents and, ultimately, I must emphasise, all other towns.

sections.label: Government data management and protection standards
sections.summary: Stringent data management and protection standards govern government and vendor data access, use and disclosure, with only legitimate officers accessing de-identified data.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: If we get the balance right – and we have to maintain public confidence – then we can truly reap the benefits that come with it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: So, I need to assure Members that we have very stringent data management and protection standards to govern the access, use and disclosure of all collected data by the Government and our vendors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In particular, only officers with legitimate use of the data will be able to access the data, and the data will be de-identified for data analysis and for planning work.

sections.label: Sensors on lamp posts data security
sections.summary: More sensors will be deployed on lamp posts, with collected data stored and used securely, as Janil Puthucheary will elaborate later.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Going forward, we will find more opportunities to deploy sensors on lamp posts, but we will ensure that the collected data is stored and used securely, and Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary will elaborate on this later.

sections.label: MaskGoWhere mask collection information
sections.summary: One team created MaskGoWhere almost overnight to give citizens up-to-date information on where to collect their masks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: One team put together MaskGoWhere almost overnight, giving citizens up-to-date information on where to collect their masks.

sections.label: Government Data Architecture delivery
sections.summary: The Government Data Architecture was established and delivered, cutting core dataset sharing from several months to four weeks, with a commitment to seven working days this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: To enable better and secure use of data, we have established the Government Data Architecture.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: It has been delivered, cutting the time needed to share the first tranche of core datasets to just four weeks when, previously, it was several months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We commit to getting it down to seven working days within this year, with more datasets for public officers to improve operations and service delivery.

sections.label: Data safeguards and annual reporting
sections.summary: Technical safeguards are built into the Government Data Architecture for consistent compliance, and an annual update on safeguarding personal data will be published starting this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Many of these technical safeguards have been built into our Government Data Architecture, ensuring that there is consistency in the compliance of these standards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We will publish an annual update on the Government's efforts in safeguarding personal data, starting with the first report later this year.

sections.label: Smart Nation showcases launch
sections.summary: Two Smart Nation showcases are launching: CityScape@URA in July and PlayScape@Science Centre in December, to give citizens interactive digital technology experiences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: To support the first experiential strategy, we are launching two major Smart Nation showcases – in July, the CityScape@URA exhibit, to give citizens an interactive experience of digital technology and, in December,	the PlayScape@Science Centre, leveraging the role that the Science Centre plays in our education, to bring the experience of being able to touch and feel and play with technology to everyone.

sections.label: SCOPE expansion for digital services
sections.summary: Over 23,000 Singaporeans have participated in SCOPE, and this year its scope expands to let the public join the entire development process of Government digital services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: To date, more than 23,000 Singaporeans have participated in SCOPE and it is not a small effort.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: This year, we will expand the scope of SCOPE in two ways.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Instead of just giving feedback on specific projects, we invite the public to join in the entire process of the development of Government digital services, from conceptualisation to deployment.

sections.label: Scams reported in 2019
sections.summary: About 9,500 scams were reported in 2019, up from over 6,000 previously, with $168 million cheated in the top 10 scam types.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: In doing so, we hope to galvanise everyone to build our Smart Nation together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
sentences.text: There were about 9,500 scams reported in 2019, up from 6,000-over cases in the previous years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
sentences.text: The total amount cheated in the top 10 types of scams came up to a staggering $168 million.

sections.label: Tech support scam losses
sections.summary: Victims lost $13.9 million in 2019, and a 65-year-old woman lost over $300,000 in a November call.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
sentences.text: Victims of tech support scams lost $13.9 million of their hard-earned savings in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
sentences.text: Just last November, a 65-year-old woman picked up a call on her landline thinking it was a customer service call from a telco.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
sentences.text: She spent over two hours on the line with the scammer and, by the end of the call, over $300,000 of her savings were wiped out from her bank account.

sections.label: Scam targeting and tactics
sections.summary: Anyone can be targeted, the elderly especially, through fake investment schemes or misuse of personal information.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Every one of us can be targeted and the elderly are especially vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Such scams and crimes typically trick individuals into handing over monies through fake investment schemes or by using their personal information to access their bank accounts.

sections.label: Banks implementing multi-factor authentication
sections.summary: Banks must implement multi-factor authentication so scammers cannot transact using only victims' user IDs and passwords.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: For example, banks must implement multi-factor authentication so that scammers cannot perform online transactions using only the user IDs and passwords of their victims.

sections.label: Freezing suspected scam accounts
sections.summary: Accounts suspected of receiving proceeds from online scams are frozen.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Third, we freeze accounts suspected of receiving the proceeds from online scams.

sections.label: TCTF operation results
sections.summary: Nine operations since TCTF's set-up solved at least 440 cases and led to over 100 regional arrests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Nine operations have been conducted since the set-up of TCTF, which resulted in at least 440 cases solved and the arrest of over 100 suspects regionally.

sections.label: Public sector retirement and training
sections.summary: The public sector extended retirement and re-employment age early and works with NTUC unions on Company Training Committees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The public sector has taken the lead in extending the retirement and re-employment age a year ahead of schedule.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: It has also been working with the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC)-affiliated unions to form Company Training Committees in its push to promote skills upgrading.

sections.label: Public officers need new skills
sections.summary: Public officers must learn new skills and sharpen existing ones amid complex problems and Auditor-General findings of recurring lapses in procurement, contract, project and facilities management.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
sentences.text: As the problems of today are becoming more complex, nuanced and require different solutions from the problems of the past, it is inevitable that our public officers will be required to learn new skills and sharpen existing skills.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
sentences.text: This is a real concern in light of the findings by the Auditor-General’s Office of recurring lapses in the bureaucracy which have raised concerns on public accountability, especially in the areas of procurement and contract management, project management and facilities management.

sections.label: PMO budget in 2016
sections.summary: The speaker states that when first entering the House in 2016, the Estimated Budget for PMO was $488 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, when I first entered this House in 2016, the Estimated Budget for PMO was $488 million.

sections.label: Future needs technology-savvy Public Service
sections.summary: Singapore's future depends on a forward-looking, technology-savvy Public Service that is wary of competition, hungry for ideas, able to learn and acts with urgency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Going forward, Singapore's future depends on the support of a forward-looking and technology-savvy Public Service, one which is wary of the speed and scale of competition, hungry for new ideas, has the capacity to learn and undertakes its tasks with a sense of urgency.

sections.label: Digital buddy volunteer programme proposed
sections.summary: The speaker proposes a "digital buddy" programme where volunteers partner those not digitally savvy to help them navigate Government digital services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: But the more "digital" Singapore's public sector becomes, the more challenging it is for those who are ill-equipped.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: I am proposing that we try out a programme called "digital buddy".

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: Such a programme would have digital buddies, who are volunteers, to partner those who are not digitally savvy to assist them in navigating Government digital services.

sections.label: Subsidies for those who cannot afford
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to aim for a position where those who want it but cannot afford it can have it through subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: But to a lower-income family, this could be a burden.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: And I would urge the Government to aim for a position whereby those who want it but cannot afford it can have it through subsidies.

sections.label: Public Service designs around people
sections.summary: The Public Service is committed to designing its services and processes around the people and businesses it serves.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The first and most fundamental mindset shift required before we even talk about all these technologies is this: the Public Service is committed to design our services and processes around the people whom we serve, around the businesses whom we serve.

sections.label: Cross-trained single officer services
sections.summary: A single officer is now cross-trained to provide services across different agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Today, we have moved on whereby a single officer has been cross-trained to provide services across different agencies.

sections.label: Public Service business partnership
sections.summary: The Public Service partners businesses to catalyse new ideas enhancing their competitiveness for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: When the Public Service partners our businesses, we are in real partnership with them to catalyse new ideas to enhance their competitiveness for Singapore.

sections.label: Regulators embracing startup culture
sections.summary: Regulators need to change their mindset and embrace startup culture so regulations evolve into a competitive advantage for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The regulators also need to change their mindset whereby they embrace the startup culture to see how regulations can evolve to become a key competitive advantage for Singapore.

sections.label: Lifelong employability for officers
sections.summary: For a 50-year Public Service career, officers must have training allowing lifelong employability, as Mr Patrick Tay mentioned.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: If we have a 50-year career for the Public Service officer, we must make sure that they have the training that can allow them to have lifelong employability, as Mr Patrick Tay has also mentioned.

sections.label: Rotating and recruiting Public Service officers
sections.summary: Public Service officers, especially leaders, will have stints beyond the Service, with systematic rotation and greater porosity in recruitment and development.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Next, we will also challenge our Public Service officers, especially those in leadership positions to go beyond the Public Service, that they will have regular stints beyond the Public Service to expose themselves to the challenges that the private sector and the people sector have.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: PSD will make sure that we organise ourselves to systematically rotate our officers within the Service, across domains and beyond the Service.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Next, we will also make sure that there is greater porosity in the Public Service, from the way we recruit people, beyond just academic qualifications, to the way we develop people and post people throughout the entire lifespan that they are here.

sections.label: Answer to Mr Louis Ng
sections.summary: The short answer to Mr Louis Ng is yes.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the short answer to Mr Louis Ng is yes.

sections.label: Young people's needs and FWAs
sections.summary: Young people consistently ask for help with housing, preschool, healthcare and achieving more FWAs.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And in our case, what is even more relevant is to reach out to the young people themselves and ask them what is it that they are looking for.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And they have been consistent in telling us: help us with housing, help us with preschool, help us with healthcare and, very importantly, help us to achieve more FWAs.

sections.label: NRF not only economic
sections.summary: NRF does not just serve economic functions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On NRF, I would just like to clarify that NRF does not just serve economic functions.

sections.label: PR population stability
sections.summary: The PR population has been quite stable.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, with regard to PRs, I think the important thing is that the PR population has been quite stable.

sections.label: Turning around policy perspective
sections.summary: Designing the MOL and equivalent apps turned around the usual perspective of fitting people into policy objectives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: It is easy, it is usual for people to think from their own perspective – how do people fit into my Ministry's policy objectives?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, from the exercise in designing the MOL and equivalent apps, we have turned this around.

sections.label: Officers walking the journey
sections.summary: Officers from different Ministries and agencies walk the entire journey imagining themselves in the shoes of the people they serve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The officers, together from different Ministries and agencies, will walk the entire journey and imagine themselves in the shoes of the people that they are going to serve.

sections.label: Empathy training for officers
sections.summary: Officers are put through another important element called empathy training or empathy design.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But there is another very important element that we are putting our officers through.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: It is what we call empathy training or empathy design.

sections.label: Municipal Service Office example
sections.summary: The Municipal Service Office (MSO) is cited as one good example.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Municipal Service Office (MSO) is one good example.
